If Alexander Graham Bell had his way, you'd answer the phone by saying, ahoy!
When the telephone was invented in 1876, there was no word for picking it up.
People weren't sure what to say. Some asked, are you there?
Bell, the inventor, wanted ahoy, like sailors calling between ships.
But his rival, Thomas Edison, suggested something else. Hello.
Back then, hello was barely a greeting. It was more like, hey, look over here!
Edison's word won, and it spread with the telephone.
Phone operators were even nicknamed, hello girls.
And Bell? He kept answering his phone with ahoy, for the rest of his life.
